pairs.why: Nearly identical wagons; B's canvas skips the extra brass rivets along the hem, so it reads slightly cleaner and smoother, like the real cards.
A keeps the canvas hem plain and smooth, while B adds rivet studs, which is the busier, texture-heavy direction the lessons marked down.
B adds rivets on the wheel and tail vane, while A's plain metal surfaces are closer to the smooth, simplified finish of the real cards.
B's tail vane has a brick-like grooved texture, while A's tail is a clean, smooth painted panel like the real cards.
The two windmills are practically the same in build, light and finish, with no meaningful difference to choose between.
B's tail vane is grooved like brick, which adds texture, while A stays smooth and simple like the real cards.
B studs the blades and rim with rivets, while A's smoother blades better match the real cards' clean, lightly detailed finish.
A covers the blades with rivets, which is more noticeable surface texture than B's slightly grooved tail, so B reads a little smoother overall.
